title: Loophole: Adversarial Agents To Stress Test Your Morality — Brendan Rappazzo, Morgan Stanley
talk_summary: The talk presents Loophole, a game where an LLM codifies a user's morals into a legal system, then adversarial agents generate loopholes and overreach cases; a judge agent auto-patches clear drafting errors or escalates genuine contradictions. It extends this to codified chatbot/agent system prompts, contract contradiction checking, and hill-climbing bill language against simulated voters.

takeaways.what_they_do: They codify rules into a system, then run one agent to find loopholes (bad but allowed) and another to find overreach (good but disallowed), with a judge resolving cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one agent is instructed to try and find loopholes in your system

takeaways.what_they_do: A judging agent checks whether a found contradiction is just an imperfect codification that can be auto-patched, or an underspecification/contradiction that must be raised to the user.
takeaways.evidence_quote: first sees can it auto patch

takeaways.technique: Hill-climb prompts against a verifiable evaluator
takeaways.what_they_do: They simulate voters/personas, score a bill against each codified contract, and iteratively change language to maximize agreement while preserving core intent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: hill climb the language of the bill such that it passed with um 52 votes

takeaways.what_they_do: They generate representative personas and use them to draft rule sets, then test proposed policies against many synthetic cases.
Natural-language rules are translated into a precise codified system prompt, then adversarial agents try to make the agent discuss forbidden topics or refuse allowed ones.
